statement: UNESCO's Ifa cultural-heritage description identifies a Yoruba divination practice interpreting a system of signs through trained babalawo, practiced in Yoruba communities and parts of the African diaspora; the institution's documentary description is contemporary heritage testimony, not an attestation of when Ifa began.

sources.citation: UNESCO Multimedia Archives, 'Ifa of the Yoruba People of Nigeria', descriptive paragraph and 2004 documentary metadata, https://www.unesco.org/archives/multimedia/document-3742
sources.author: UNESCO / Ifa Group of Oyo
sources.access_note: Full public description and documentary metadata (publisher Ifa Group of Oyo, 2004) were read. Video content not viewed; statements are UNESCO's public account, not direct analysis of Odu Ifa verses.

does_not_demonstrate: A 2004 documentary or 2008 heritage inscription does not date the origins of Ifa practice.
The institutional synopsis does not verify the content of a particular oral divination verse.
Yoruba and diaspora communities can differ; the description does not demonstrate a uniform worldwide practice.
adversarial_counter: Specific ritual content and diversity across Yoruba communities would require source-identified practitioner testimony and oral-text recordings.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
